findings.title: Call to missing no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate invokes isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method with that name in the class hierarchy is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). Because no no-arg overload exists, this file cannot compile. The call should likely pass context.getUser() or a no-arg overload must be added.

findings.title: Passkeys no longer rendered for initial first-factor login when no user is selected
findings.body: The new condition uses isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), whose implementation requires user != null. This replaces the previous behavior where fillContextForm was called exactly when context.getUser() == null for normal first-factor authentication. On a fresh login without an already selected user, webauthnAuth.fillContextForm is now skipped, so the login page lacks the conditional webauthn/passkey challenge and discoverable-passkey auto-login is broken. The same null-user exclusion also affects challenge(...) at line 137 after failed first-factor submissions. The fill should be based on webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled(), independent of whether context.getUser() is set.
